notes: Only original n_o, es_value_o and pval_value_o are assigned. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Title matches the reference. Rendered PDF page 4 confirms layout and that canonical text "p b" denotes printed p <; the 3 in t(60 3) is footnote marker 3, not a df digit. The locator is only p. 4, description and study identifiers are null. Candidate tests on printed p. 141: Target Race × Communication Positivity B = − .32, SE = .10, t(60) = 3.11, p < .01; Target Race × IMS × Communication Positivity B = .26, SE = .09, t(60) = 2.88, p < .01; low-IMS target-race simple effects for negative communications B = .65, SE = .16, t(60) = 4.10 and positive communications B = −.27, SE = .06, t(60) = −4.45, both ps < .0001; positivity slope for Black targets B = .78, SE = .22, t(60) = 3.61, p < .001; positivity slope for White targets B = −.54, SE = .11, t(60) = 4.92, p < .0001 (sign retained as printed); bottom-panel simple effects all ps > .26. Footnote 3 additionally gives the uncontrolled three-way interaction p < .07. Do not choose among these without a target description. The source prints B and t for these tests, not Cohen's f^2; no conversion or assumption about coefficient standardization made. Candidate N =85 is explicitly the post-IMS/EMS exclusion base; controlled attitude analyses have nine additional missing pre-test records. No subtraction-derived analytic N or df-derived N recorded, and no mutually exclusive final group counts are printed. Page 4 discussion also gives r = − .56 for IMS and explicit racial attitudes, another distinct statistic. The last results sentence labels the bottom panel "low" IMS, whereas the decomposition and figure label it high IMS; this source inconsistency is retained, not resolved by inference.
